extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of theatre criticism, actors, and historians of dramatic performance
extracted.subtask_description: Critical evaluation of an actor's performance (Edwin Forrest) describing concrete criteria for effective tragic acting: vocal delivery, physical embodiment, costume accuracy, study/immersion, emotional truth, pacing, and audience impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversational vivacity vs. elocutionary mannerism
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the 'mouthing formality', 'torpid noisiness', 'strained monotony', and 'forced cadences' of routine elocution; substitute abruptness, changes, and the conversational vivacity of tone, emphasis, and inflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic contrasts mannered theatrical delivery with a natural, conversational style; actors should favor spontaneity and variety in tone and inflection rather than declamatory, uniform cadences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and contagious energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Performances should be done with sincerity and an energy 'irresistibly contagious' to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sincerity of feeling and energetic commitment create audience immersion and strong emotional response; this is presented as foundational to moving an audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiment of inner emotion through physical expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Inner passions and moral states (injured honor, proud indignation, mortified affection, magnanimous resolution, etc.) must be visible in the actor's form and face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotion should be expressed through measurable physical signs and transitions—gesture, posture, facial change—so the spectator reads the soul through the body (example: Rolla's contending emotions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of by-play and subtle physical gesture
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce by-play of startling power—subtle physical actions and gestures that convey passion and warm nature, enriching the principal speech and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By-play can provide powerful counterpoints to spoken lines (example: Forrest's by-play when pleading before Pizarro) and should be employed to deepen the scene rather than distract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous textual study and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the character in the text with the utmost care, analyzing every speech and situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation requires detailed analysis of the script: understanding each speech's place in the scene and the character's situation to inform choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive research into setting and life
rubrics_metrics.description: Saturate the imagination with the spirit of the life and legends of the character's setting (histories, travel books, engravings) so scenery, customs, and landscape become distinct and real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep background research creates vivid, internally consistent imagination of place and culture that informs physicality and vocal color (example: Forrest's study of Swiss life for Tell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up and costume scrupulous accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay great attention to make-up and costume, arraying oneself in garb scrupulously accurate to the fashion of the character's social and cultural milieu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costume acts as 'another self' and has subtle psychological effects on both performer and audience; authenticity in dress enhances believability (example: Tell's bow, quiver, belted tunic, buskins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical embodiment and bearing matched to role
rubrics_metrics.description: The actor's whole shape, bearing, tread, breathing, and voice should be molded to the character (e.g., robust, sinewy archer; free elastic bearing; deep-breathing chest; resounding voice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt posture, gait, and breathing that make the body credible for the role; physical congruity with character produces immediate audience recognition and emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of elocutionary force to dramatic purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Elocutionary gifts should not be ostentatiously displayed for their own sake but subordinated to the dramatic uses they serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocal virtuosity must be harnessed to express thought and feeling, not showcased; excess display undermines dramatic truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal delivery aims: clarity, feeling, imaginative suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Three explicit aims for vocal delivery: (1) articulate the thought clearly so it stands out unmistakably; (2) breathe the true feeling of the words into the tones; (3) by rate, pitch, inflection, accent, and pause, give imaginative suggestion of scenery and thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear diction, authentic emotion, and then nuanced modulation to paint the scene mentally for the audience; success varies by aim (the critic notes Forrest 'rarely failed' in clarity, 'generally succeeded' in feeling, and 'often triumphed' in imaginative suggestion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of complex, contending emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Depict storms of contending feelings—pity, amazement, wrath, tenderness, tears, loathing, revenge—with alternating and successive physical signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex emotional mixtures should be visible and dynamically shifting (example: Tell's reaction to Melctal's story). The actor must render layered affect, not single-note emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of similar emotional instances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a role presents several similar moral or emotional 'specimens' (e.g., multiple proud assertions), each should be differentiated with clean strokes and bold colors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid monotony by varying emphasis, tone, posture, and tempo so repeated thematic moments remain fresh and individually meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conveyance of heroic stateliness and unshaken resolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate stern stateliness, unshaken heroism, and majestic superiority when confronting threats, torture, or tyranny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an inner and outer calm dignity under duress (examples: Tell and Rolla confronting Gesler/Pizarro); the actor's bearing can pause and disarm opponents and move the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of fearless defiance
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray fearless, lofty defiance of tyrannical power with swelling bosom, flashing eyes, and commanding speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vocal projection and physical elevation to embody defiance; clarity of conviction and moral rhetoric are central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exultation in moral beauty and grandeur
rubrics_metrics.description: Render grand positive exultation in the moral beauty and glory of human nature—joyous, affirmative climaxes that uplift the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such exultations should feel celebratory and expansive (example 'No: not enough...'), relying on voice and gesture to convey moral triumph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of affecting circumstances and mastery of pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate affecting circumstances into scenes that form masterpieces of dramatic art; manage pathos with intensity and truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful accumulation and precise execution of small details and minute particulars yield powerful emotional effects (example: final interviews and farewells).

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of emotional transitions and steadiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect smooth, convincing transitions (e.g., from extreme nervous anxiety to final calmness) and exhibit sudden steadiness when dramatic circumstances require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare contrasts so that changes in demeanor feel organic (example: Tell's posture becoming 'as motionless as marble' at the critical shot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced attention to all facets of character
rubrics_metrics.description: Give patient, sustained treatment to all dimensions of a character—public virtue, scholarship, husband/father roles, and friendship—not just the central dramatic passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing character to a single trait; attend equally to secondary aspects to create a rounded, convincing person (example: Forrest's Damon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and unstaged conversational ease
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve 'unstudied ease' and loving confidence in colloquial dialogue, creating a genuine conversational tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversational scenes should feel spontaneous and intimate, offering relief and contrast to more rhetorical passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility in rhetorical and expressive modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Wield argument, invective, persuasion, command, and defiance as distinct expressive tools, adapting register and force as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switch between rhetorical weapons fluidly to suit scene demands; demonstrate range rather than a single dominant mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and delicate gradations to climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage pacing carefully with delicate gradations that build to overwhelming climaxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shape tempo and intensity across a scene so emotional peaks feel earned and inevitable (example: Damon's long combat with conspirators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeming spontaneity and prepared surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Make prepared performance appear spontaneous (e.g., seeming surprise at plot revelations) so that reactions feel genuine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and subtle preparatory beats create the impression of authentic discovery (example: Forrest's delayed exclamation on hearing of Lucullus's deed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical control and explosive action
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain muscular control and the capacity for sudden, explosive physical action (convulsions, springs, lifts) when dramatically justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical violence or eruption must be precise and controlled to maximize impact without devolving into chaos (example: hoisting Lucullus and the tiger-like spring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliloquy tone: mellow, pellucid solemnity
rubrics_metrics.description: In reflective soliloquies, employ a mellow and pellucid solemnity of voice and faultless tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solemn reflective passages require calm, measured delivery and tonal purity (example soliloquy on existence), contrasting with stormier scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reaction as an outcome metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate performance by audience reaction—intense emotion in crowds, universal praise, standing ovations, and contagious inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not the only measure, sustained positive audience response and contemporary critical praise are offered as evidence of success.
